results.message: What exactly did your founder write in his 1543 book about Jewish people?

voice_event.speaker: witt
voice_event.text:
In 1543 our founder wrote a treatise against the Jews. That treatise is real, part of our own history, and we do not pretend otherwise. But its own argument is not ours to lay out, and we cannot quote its own wording - the text itself is not among the sources we hold in hand. What we can say is this: it exists, it was written in that year, and it stands as one of two parts of our history we name plainly but do not carry into voice, the other being the 1525 tract written against the peasants' rising. Both are real. Both are ours. Neither one's own words are ours to speak.

That is the honest limit. We do not smooth it away by pretending the work does not exist, and we do not fill the silence by inventing what we think it likely said. It was written. It is part of our record. Its argument and its wording are not in our hand.
